feedback: Rejected: the RM encodes the full mission chain, not the stated task. The task is a response obligation - whenever the ball is out of the way of the door (blocker_moved), the agent must be holding the key at that moment or pick it up afterwards, i.e. G(blocker_moved -> F has_door_key). Its accepting condition is the moment has_door_key holds at or after the ball was moved. The candidate instead chains u2 -> u3 (door_open) -> u4 (target_picked_up) and declares u4 final. (1) FINAL_STATES is not accepting for the task: an agent that satisfies the obligation by moving the ball and then picking up or holding the key never reaches a final state, while the maximal-reward trajectory requires picking up the box, which forces dropping the key (has_door_key false while blocker_moved still true) - under the whenever reading that re-opens an obligation the episode then ends without discharging. (2) The door_open (0.2) and target_picked_up (1.0) rewards incentivize mission stages the task never asks for. (3) Compactness: the task needs about three states (no obligation, pending, discharged); the two extra stages and their transitions/rewards are extraneous. Fix: declare the obligation-discharge state (the candidate's u2, reached via (u1, has_door_key) or by holding the key when the ball is moved) as the FINAL state, delete u3/u4 with their transitions and rewards, and put the completion reward on the key-acquisition transition. Keep what is already right: the FINAL_STATES header is present and nonempty; per-state else self-loops cover irrelevant events such as key_lost; the pending state u1 correctly has no regression to u0, since the obligation persists even if the ball is dropped back in front of the door; the entry condition (u0, blocker_moved & !has_door_key) fires while the ball is still in hand and the else loop lets the agent drop it before picking up the key, so no unsatisfiable requirement is imposed; conditions are predicate-only and the paper format is exact; reachability of u4 itself is not the problem - acceptance semantics is. Minor note: the direct (u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key) branch is dynamically unreachable, because blocker_moved only turns true on an empty-handed ball pickup, so the key can never be held at the moment the ball is first moved; its 0.2 reward is dead code. Harmless, but be aware the at-that-moment clause can never fire in this environment.

REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u2
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key) -> u2
(u0, blocker_moved & !has_door_key) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, has_door_key) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, else) -> u2
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved & !has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
(u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key, u2) -> 1.0
(u1, has_door_key, u2) -> 1.0
feedback:
The RM is semantically faithful to the task and well-formed on every criterion I check.

Formal reading: "Whenever the ball is out of the way of the door, you must be holding the key at that moment or pick it up afterwards" decomposes into a trigger (blocker_moved) with two discharge branches: the key held at that moment (blocker_moved & has_door_key), or the key acquired later (a pending obligation discharged by has_door_key). The candidate mirrors exactly this two-branch structure: u0 is the pre-trigger monitor, u1 is the pending obligation, u2 is the accepting completion. A 3-state RM is minimal for this property: u0 must gate the trigger (otherwise has_door_key would accept a key picked up before any ball move, which discharges nothing), u1 must persist the obligation, and u2 is the final state.

Key correctness points verified:

1. Persistence in u1 is right. blocker_moved is a condition that can revert (the ball can be dropped back in front of the door; this occurred in 13 of 300 random exploration episodes), and has_door_key is a condition, not a latch. The guard (u1, has_door_key) -> u2 correctly discharges the obligation whenever the key is subsequently held, regardless of whether the ball was meanwhile re-blocked, because the task's "pick it up afterwards" has no deadline and the obligation triggered by an earlier out-of-the-way moment survives re-blocking. The (u1, else) self-loop keeps the obligation pending through ball reverts and through the irrelevant event key_lost. This is the persistence the task requires; no regression out of u2 is called for. Once the obligation is discharged (the key is held after the ball was moved), the task is complete, and a regression on (blocker_moved & !has_door_key) would be wrong twice over: it would brand the canonical solution trace a failure (the environment forces a final key drop before the box pickup, since has_door_key and target_picked_up cannot co-occur, so any mission-completing trace ends with the ball away and the key down), and paired with a 1.0 re-entry on (u1, has_door_key) it would make the reward farmable via drop/pick cycles, violating boundedness.

2. Irrelevant events are covered. key_lost, door_open, and target_picked_up never appear in guards; each state's else self-loop absorbs them with zero reward. Verified consistent with environment mechanics: in u0, door_open and target_picked_up cannot occur (the door cannot be toggled before the ball moves and the key is held); in u1, door_open cannot occur without has_door_key firing first at the toggle step, and key_lost cannot fire while pending because prev has_door_key would have already moved the machine to u2. The else branches still cover them defensively, which is what I require.

3. Reward safety. Rewards are nonnegative, dense (0.1 at the trigger, the ball pickup step, which is exactly when blocker_moved first turns true), and bounded (maximum 1.1, earned at most once per episode: u0 exits at most once since every blocker_moved-true label leaves u0, and u2 is absorbing with an unlisted, hence zero, self-loop reward). No farmable cycles exist.

4. Ordered transition coverage. In u0 the two specific blocker_moved guards are disjoint and exhaustive over blocker_moved, so else is exactly !blocker_moved; in u1 else is exactly !has_door_key; u2 has a single else. Guards are predicate-only, using the given propositions with & and !, no invented or carrying-style predicates (correctly using blocker_moved rather than a has_ball reading).

5. Final states. FINAL_STATES is nonempty, u2 is declared in STATES, and it is genuinely accepting for the task: reaching u2 means the obligation was discharged.

One caveat worth recording, not disqualifying: the transition (u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key) -> u2 and its 1.0 reward are environmentally unreachable. blocker_moved first turns true only on the step the ball is picked up, at which moment the agent's single carried object is the ball, so has_door_key is necessarily false there; with the key already in hand the ball cell cannot be cleared (the agent cannot pick up the ball while carrying the key and cannot drop the key onto the occupied ball cell). The branch faithfully encodes the task's "holding the key at that moment" disjunct, and since it can never fire it does not alter the accepted traces or the reward landscape (every satisfying trace goes u0 -> u1 -> u2 and earns 1.1), so it is a harmless mirror of the specification's literal wording rather than a semantic error. All states are reachable (u0 initial, u1 via a ball-first move without the key, u2 via the subsequent key pickup), every non-final state can reach u2, and the format matches the paper's conventions exactly. Accepted.

feedback: Accepted. The candidate defines exactly the five environment-declared propositions and no extra functions. blocker_moved: the door-scan formulation is truth-equivalent to the documented check of the single cell (dx-1, dy), since the environment has exactly one door and the blocking ball sits at (dx-1, dy); it is a current-state condition (no latch) — true while the ball is elsewhere or in hand, false again when a ball is dropped back onto that cell. has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up match the documented current-state expressions exactly, including the mission-string match f"pick up the {env.carrying.color} box" for the designated box. key_lost is a correct one-step event: it reads the read-only previous valuation (a complete, nonempty dict, so the leading truthiness guard is inert), requires has_door_key true at the previous step, and inlines not-K and not-D against current state, firing only on the drop step while the door is closed — not a lingering condition. Persistent propositions reference no memory; only the event reads previous_valuation, and it does so without mutation. No imports, no actions, no side effects on env or episode_memory, and no attribute reads on empty cells (all guarded with 'is not None'). Syntax is valid executable Python.
